title: Level 5 (World Class) - B-30
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 3NT. West's spade lead is won by South. The only possible problem is a 4-0 club break and a 5-2 spade break. South may be able to guard against this distribution by playing for a compound suicide squeeze.

South should start by cashing a high club from the closed hand. The ♣Q will be needed as a later dummy entry. When East turns up with a club stopper, South exits the ♠6. West must cash his spades or South will be able to establish his ninth trick in clubs.

On the second last spade, East will have to abandon either hearts or diamonds. South will have to guess which suit East is no longer guarding. West has 5 known cards (5 spades) to East's 6 known cards (2 spades and 4 clubs). West is thus a favourite to have been dealt at least as many hearts and diamonds as East. West's most likely original shape is, therefore, 5440.

If East discards a diamond, so does South. On the last spade, a club is thrown from both hands. South can now succeed on a double squeeze (hearts being guarded by both defenders) regardless of what West returns.

On a heart return, for example, South wins the ♥A and unblocks the clubs. South returns to the closed hand in diamonds. The other diamond honour will squeeze East in hearts and clubs. A heart discard will leave West with the only defensive heart guard. South's remaining top club will then squeeze West in hearts and diamonds.

If, instead, East abandons hearts on the second last spade, South also pitches a heart. On the last spade a diamond is pitched from dummy and a club is thrown from the closed hand.

Again there will be a double squeeze, this time with diamonds guarded by both defenders. Assume that West switches to diamonds and South wins. South cashes the ♥A and the remaining club honour in the closed hand. A club to the ♣Q will squeeze West in hearts and diamonds. A diamond discard will leave East with the only defensive diamond guard. The ♥K will then squeeze East in diamonds and clubs.
